behaviors.description: Construct default, named and user installation objects and reject an unknown name.
behaviors.preconditions: Actual compiled default location and configured named alt location in private namespace.
behaviors.expected: Exact paths, IDs and user flags; unknown name returns NULL with error.

behaviors.preconditions: Named alt declares display name, priority 25 and network storage.
behaviors.expected: Public getters return exactly the configured values.

behaviors.description: Verify a reachable configured installation, then obstruct its configured path itself with a regular file.
behaviors.preconditions: Default, alt and the control installation are initially reachable inside the disposable namespace.
behaviors.expected: Control constructor succeeds and enumeration initially includes all three system installations. After obstruction, the control constructor fails and enumeration returns exactly default and alt, excluding control and user.

behaviors.description: Install and query distinct commits through selected public library objects.
behaviors.preconditions: Direct-root transactions install system A and named/user B.
behaviors.expected: Each installed-ref lookup reports its own commit, including after reopening the default object.

behaviors.description: Construct a non-user installation for the populated named path.
behaviors.preconditions: Default A and named B, each with app/runtime deployments.
behaviors.expected: Custom object reports requested path and non-user flag; exact app/runtime set and B commit differ from default A.

behaviors.description: Query installed metadata and typed membership in a named installation.
behaviors.preconditions: Named app B and runtime; default A and user B remain separate.
behaviors.expected: Exact app/runtime sets and empty kind results after removal; exact application metadata and named deployment location.

mappings.rationale: Constructors report exact compiled/configured paths, default/alt IDs and non-user flags; the actual root-user constructor is separately checked.
Display name, priority 25 and NETWORK enum match the explicit named configuration.

The reachable control constructor and three-member enumeration succeed first. Replacing the configured control path itself with a regular file makes its public constructor fail; enumeration then contains exactly default and alt and excludes the control and user installations.
Library-created system A versus user/named B are queried through their own objects; each transaction returns its supplied installation object.
new_for_path(FALSE) reports alt path/non-user and enumerates exact alt app/runtime; B differs from default A.
Typed results contain exactly app/runtime and become empty after corresponding removal; complete four-key Application metadata is checked against fixture identity.

notes: Every target call enters two disposable bubblewrap user/mount namespace layers. The outer root maps only to the invoking host UID; inner root maps only to outer root. Inherited host mounts are locked read-only, checked by a denied bind-remount before every target call. Private PID/network namespaces and writable installation state are case-local; generated state is removed after each case while command evidence is retained.

Target environment keys BLACKBOX_SYSTEM_INSTALL_DIR and BLACKBOX_SYSTEM_CONFIG_DIR specify the expected compiled defaults; their reference-build defaults are /var/local/lib/flatpak and /usr/local/etc/flatpak. The namespace mounts private data at those paths, and CLI/C-client assertions still check the target's actual default location. These keys never become FLATPAK_SYSTEM_DIR or FLATPAK_CONFIG_DIR redirects. Set them under the target JSON environment object, not the host shell environment.

Readonly exposure includes only the suite directory, selected target executables, configured helpers and LD_LIBRARY_PATH directories. Uninstalled targets can explicitly add colon-separated absolute paths with BLACKBOX_TARGET_READONLY_PATHS in the target environment. No repository ancestor is inferred. Paths that cover private namespace roots or overlap protected installation/service content are rejected, including symlink aliases.

CLI deployment location checks use the public returned location, verify containment in the selected public installation base, locate the controlled bin/blackbox-probe payload there and execute it to distinguish A from B. They never construct a deployment path from a ref or commit, and never recursively search a general installation root for content.

Direct-root mutations may satisfy explicitly selected installation outcomes. These cases do not assert polkit authorization, non-root helper behavior, or multiple-user access. No requirement demanding those outcomes is mapped.
The named override case intentionally asserts the documented isolation contract; the reference target currently fails it, so that option receives no verified credit from that case.
